earlier_scan.source_named: Shào Míngyuán 2018, pp. 365-371 (sole reference on Glottolog dong1304; Chinese-language survey sketch of Dongna Tibetan); not found online

sources.citation: Tournadre, Nicolas & Hiroyuki Suzuki. 2023. The Tibetic Languages: an introduction to the family of languages derived from Old Tibetan. Villejuif: LACITO Publications (open access). Part 2, ch.9 (NE section)
sources.note: Dungnak and rTarmnyik 'recently discovered in Gansu by Shao Mingyuan in 2012... need further research', possibly Kham enclaves in Amdo; 'See Shao (2018) for details'. Nothing Dungnak-specific on prosody. Areal statement sec. 9.5.6: Amdo (NE section) 'does not have distinctive suprasegmental features. However, the position of stress may affect some phonetic realisations.' — not attributable to Dongna, whose affiliation the authors leave open.

sources.citation: 中山大学中文系 faculty page of 邵明园 (publication list), https://chinese.sysu.edu.cn/teacher/508
sources.note: Used to check for a separate Dongna phonology article: none listed (Dongna items are the 2018 book, the 2021 evidentiality chapter, the 2022 JCL clause-chain paper).

sources.citation: 邵明園 [Shao Mingyuan]. 2019. 古藏文的系動詞 [Copulas in Old Tibetan]. Language and Linguistics 20(4). doi:10.1075/lali.00039.sha (open access)
sources.note: Nothing; fn.19 (p.440) only a sociolinguistic note: Dongna <mdung.nag> Tibetan, Sunan county, c.2500 people, ~20 elderly speakers, overall Amdo-like with some Khams-like sound changes.

sources.citation: 鈴木博之 [Suzuki, Hiroyuki]. 2019. <書評> 邵明園(著)《河西走廊瀕危藏語東納話研究》廣州: 中山大學出版社, 2018年, 10+450pp. 京都大学言語学研究 (Kyoto University Linguistic Research) 38: 65-73. doi:10.14989/250192
sources.note: Review sec.2 (pp.66-68) summarises Shao's phonology chapter: consonant/cluster notation, no vowel-length opposition (Shao p.29), 'special changes' list includes '第2音節の弱化' (weakening of the 2nd syllable), word-internal resyllabification of cluster pre-initials; p.71: Shao's focus-structure section '文の構造のみならず、ストレスにも言及している' (mentions stress as well as sentence structure). No statement of word-stress position; tone not discussed in the review.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (zh) '东纳话' and Wikipedia (en) 'mDungnag language' (accessed 2026-09-17), both sourced solely to Shao 2018 and Suzuki 2019
sources.note: '东纳话没有声调' / 'mDungnag is a non-tonal language' (citing Shao 2018). Nothing on stress. Second-hand tertiary source.

sources.note: The only descriptive grammar of Dongna (Glottolog's sole reference; Hammarström holds a scan ''). Its phonology chapter is where any statement on tone/stress (声调/重音/习惯调) would be; Wikipedia's 'no tones' and Suzuki's 'second-syllable weakening' both trace to it.
